items.title: ST-HVG-Parse: request ordered X_hvg gene names and release preprocessing provenance
items.body:
### Reproducibility request for ST-HVG-Parse

Could you publish the **ordered 2000 gene names corresponding to `obsm["X_hvg"]`**, or a canonical mask plus its original ordered gene universe, for the current ST-HVG-Parse release?

This is a Parse-specific follow-up to #279. Model integration remains on hold: partial or all-zero numeric matches do not establish all feature identities.

### Pinned artifacts

- [ST-HVG-Parse](https://huggingface.co/arcinstitute/ST-HVG-Parse/tree/827df657cd87063026d2abefd73e99036755ac1b), revision `827df657cd87063026d2abefd73e99036755ac1b`.
- [State-Parse-Filtered](https://huggingface.co/datasets/arcinstitute/State-Parse-Filtered/tree/7e6acd905c412094330710a721a46280b7ef53de), revision `7e6acd905c412094330710a721a46280b7ef53de`.
- Code: `state v0.11.1`, `cell-load v0.10.4`, `state-reproduce v0.1.0`.

The model's `fewshot/split_4/var_dims.pkl` reports 2000 input/output/HVG dimensions, but 18308 gene names. Those names match the processed file's full `var/_index`. The full file has `X_hvg.shape=(9697974,2000)`, no HVG mask in `var`, and empty `uns`; the inspected split-4 real evaluation file uses names `0..1999`. We have not downloaded the Parse checkpoint body or exhaustively searched every evaluation file.

The public baseline [training entry point](https://github.com/ArcInstitute/state-reproduce/blob/v0.1.0/baselines/state_sets_reproduce/train/__main__.py) reads an internal `parse_hvg_names.txt`; it was not found in the complete public tag archive.

### New bounded numeric investigation

We located Parse's [official original dataset](https://www.parsebiosciences.com/datasets/10-million-human-pbmcs-in-a-single-experiment/), specifically [the 20260203 h5ad ZIP](https://parse-wget.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/10m/10M_PBMC_12donor_90cytokines_h5ad_20260203.zip), whose raw count matrix has 40352 named genes.

The original and Arc files have different row orders. We aligned selected rows and checked **barcode, sample and donor** individually. In a 64-cell calibration, float32 CSR `normalize_total(target_sum=3320)` followed by `log1p` exactly matched all 1171712 values for the 18308 common genes. The same frozen transformation then matched every common-gene value in 11264 recovery cells and 1024 fresh, disjoint validation cells. **3320 is an observed numeric bridge, not a claim about the official release recipe.** Actual raw-count row sums were used, not `obs.tscp_count`.

Searching the complete 40352-gene catalog on the 11264 recovery cells produced:
- 1931 columns with one exact numeric candidate; all passed the subsequent 1024-cell frozen-candidate validation, with no duplicate genes.
- 69 ambiguous columns: 55 all-zero vectors and 14 supported by one nonzero cell.
- 0 unmatched columns.

All 1931 unique anchors follow the original `var` order. Order constraints give 32 additional conditional single candidates and leave 37 ambiguous, but **we have not accepted those structural candidates or created a canonical 2000-gene map**. Earlier 64-cell-only matches were sample-limited and some were invalidated by expansion. Full source-object hashes have not been verified; this investigation uses recorded HTTP byte ranges.

### Release provenance and treatment-label questions

The fixed [preprocess_train command](https://github.com/ArcInstitute/state/blob/v0.11.1/src/state/_cli/_tx/_preprocess_train.py) applies normalization without an explicit target, log1p, default-flavor HVG selection, then a boolean `highly_variable` subset preserving `var` order. It retains the mask in the full output. This does not establish the actual release pipeline.

We also observed **296 selected cells** with identical barcode/sample/donor but different original versus Arc `cytokine` fields:

| Original 20260203 field | Arc field |
|---|---|
| Megalin | C3a |
| IL-18Ra | IL-18 |
| LAP-TGF-beta1 | TGF-beta1 |

These are not being treated as synonyms. Could you confirm which field/version represents the actual administered reagents and whether these differences are annotation corrections?

Could you also provide:
1. The canonical ordered 2000 gene list/mask and matching ST-SE-Parse expression-decoder list.
2. The HVG selection cell pool, original gene universe, flavor, parameters, software version, and any subsequent gene filtering/reordering.
3. The actual normalization target and preprocessing steps for this release.

An official small gene-list asset would resolve the remaining identity uncertainty without relying on expected cytokine biology.

items.title: Request: ordered 2000-HVG gene name list for ST-HVG-* releases (obsm['X_hvg'] is positionally consumed by tx infer)
items.body:
### Summary

We are using the released **ST-HVG-Tahoe** checkpoint (`fewshot/state_generalization_X_hvg`) for downstream perturbation-direction analysis, and ran into a reproducibility gap: `state tx infer --embed-key X_hvg` consumes `adata.obsm["X_hvg"]` **positionally**, but the release does not include the gene-name list for the 2000 HVG columns. `var_dims.pkl` carries the full 62,710-gene `gene_names`, and the eval artifacts (`adata_real.h5ad` var_names, `*_de.csv` feature columns) all use integer indices `0..1999`.

Could you publish the ordered 2000-HVG gene list (e.g., `hvg_names.json` / `.csv`) for **ST-HVG-Tahoe** (and ideally the same for ST-HVG-Parse / ST-HVG-Replogle) to the HF repos? A one-file addition would make the fewshot checkpoints directly usable for inference.

### What we already checked (so you don't have to)

- `checkpoints/*.ckpt` hyper_parameters / state_dict — no HVG names
- `var_dims.pkl` — only `gene_names` (62,710), `hvg_dim: 2000`
- `fewshot/generalization.toml` — split config only
- `eval_best.ckpt/adata_real.h5ad` — `var/_index` = `0..1999`
- `eval_best.ckpt/*_real_de.csv` — `feature` = `0..1999`
- HF `tahoebio/Tahoe-100M` `metadata/gene_metadata.parquet` (62,710 rows) — no HVG flag
- `state tx preprocess_train --num_hvgs 2000` — we know the recipe (`sc.pp.highly_variable_genes`), but the training pool is not public, so exact reproduction isn't possible

### Context

Our use case is ESCC (esophageal carcinoma) treatment-response hypothesis validation with DSPIN/CausCell; ST-HVG-Tahoe would serve as the third-engine arbitrator (chemo drugs like 5-FU/Paclitaxel are in `pert_onehot_map`). Until the list is available we cannot construct a positionally-correct `X_hvg`, and we will not guess.

Thanks!

items.title: Store and Access HVG Gene Names in AnnData
items.body:
## Summary

This PR enhances STATE's handling of highly variable genes (HVGs) by storing gene names directly in AnnData objects alongside the HVG expression matrix. This enables downstream tools like `pdex` to properly map predictions back to gene IDs without requiring additional metadata files.

## Changes

### Core Infrastructure
- **New constants module** (`src/state/tx/constants.py`): Centralizes shared constants for TX workflows
- **New HVG utilities** (`src/state/tx/utils/hvg.py`): Provides functions to retrieve and validate HVG gene names with fallback mechanisms

### Preprocessing Enhancements
- **Enhanced `preprocess_train`**: Now stores HVG gene names in `adata.uns["X_hvg_var_names"]` alongside the HVG matrix in `adata.obsm["X_hvg"]`
- **Updated inference preprocessing**: Added validation and warning when HVG names are missing

### CLI Improvements
- **Enhanced `infer` command**: Added `--verbose` flag to show HVG name mapping details and status reporting
- **Updated `predict` command**: Preserves HVG names in prediction outputs

### Documentation & Migration
- **New repository guidelines** (`AGENTS.md`): Comprehensive development guidelines
- **Migration guide** (`docs/migration/hvg_var_names.md`): Backward compatibility notes and backfill script for existing data
- **Updated README**: Added section on accessing HVG gene names

### Testing
- **New test suites**: Comprehensive tests for HVG utilities, inference pipeline, prediction outputs, and preprocessing workflows
- **All existing tests pass**: No regressions introduced

## Backward Compatibility

This change is fully backward compatible:
- **Existing preprocessed data**: Inference commands continue working without modification
- **Non-blocking warnings**: Users are notified when HVG names are missing but execution proceeds
- **Fallback mechanisms**: Code can still recover gene names from `adata.var.highly_variable` when available
- **No API changes**: Existing workflows continue functioning unchanged

## Usage Examples

### Accessing HVG Gene Names
```python
import anndata as ad

# After preprocessing with latest STATE version
adata = ad.read_h5ad("preprocessed.h5ad")
hvg_names = adata.uns.get("X_hvg_var_names")

# Construct downstream AnnData for tools like pdex
adata_for_pdex = ad.AnnData(
    X=adata.obsm["X_hvg"],
    obs=adata.obs,
    var=pd.DataFrame(index=hvg_names),
)
```

### Backfilling Existing Data
For pre-existing datasets, use the provided backfill script to add HVG names to existing files.

## Technical Details

- HVG names are stored as NumPy arrays of Python strings for h5ad compatibility
- Naming convention `{obsm_key}_var_names` allows extension to other embedding types
- Comprehensive validation ensures gene name arrays match embedding dimensions
- Fallback logic prioritizes explicit uns keys over implicit var-based recovery

## Testing

- All existing tests pass
- New test coverage includes:
  - HVG name retrieval with multiple fallback scenarios
  - Inference pipeline preservation of HVG metadata
  - Prediction output includes HVG names
  - Preprocessing correctly stores HVG names
  - End-to-end workflow validation

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Low risk**: Fully backward compatible with existing workflows
- **Data integrity**: Validation ensures HVG name arrays match embedding dimensions
- **Performance**: Minimal overhead - only stores additional metadata
- **Migration**: Clear documentation and backfill scripts provided

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Implements explicit storage and propagation of highly variable gene (HVG) names to enable downstream mapping and compatibility.
> 
> - **Core**: Add `state/tx/constants.py` and `state/tx/utils/hvg.py` for HVG name keys, retrieval, fallbacks, and validation
> - **Preprocessing**: `tx preprocess_train` now writes HVG matrix to `obsm['X_hvg']` and names to `uns['X_hvg_var_names']`; `tx preprocess_infer` logs presence and warns if missing
> - **Inference/Prediction**: `tx infer` gains `--verbose`, reports HVG mapping status, and writes `uns['X_hvg_var_names']` to outputs; `tx predict` includes HVG names in both `adata_pred` and `adata_real`
> - **Dataset**: `scgpt_perturbation_dataset.py` defaults to reading HVG names from `uns['X_hvg_var_names']`
> - **Docs**: Update `README.md` with HVG access examples and CLI fixes; add migration guide `docs/migration/hvg_var_names.md`; add `AGENTS.md`
> - **Tests**: New tests for HVG utilities, preprocess (train/infer), inference pipeline, and prediction outputs
> 
> <sup>Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 98d205db2eb9fdb69e02ea822552de969bb2deaf. This will update automatically on new commits. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).</sup>

items.title: ST training with and without SE embeddings
items.body:
Dear maintainers,

The published tutorials for `state tx train` use `data.kwargs.embed_key=X_hvg \` so the ST model is trained using 2000 HVGs.

But in the preprint, it is mentioned that ST can be trained using a combined loss on both SE embeddings and the gene expression values, where loss in the gene expression space is downweighted by 0.1.

I searched through the code and couldn't find a way to train ST from scratch using this technique. I have some questions related to this:

1. If I use `state tx train data.kwargs.embed_key=X_state` is the loss only on the SE embeddings? 
2. If yes, how do I implement the combined loss and the latent-to-gene decoder? `output_space`? There are also many decoder-related arguments which are not clearly explained.
3. The default setting of `decoder_loss_weight` is set to 1.0 rather than 0.1 as in the preprint, which confused me further.

In the end I want to train ST models with and without SE embeddings, and this is currently not explained in the tutorial. I would really appreciate your help in this.

items.title: rename X_hvg within a batch to X_gene

items.title: Issues with running the pretrained ST-Tahoe model
items.body:
Thanks for releasing this great model and making the code available! We're excited to try it out, but we encountered a few issues when attempting to load and run inference using the provided infrastructure. We'd really appreciate any clarification or guidance you could provide.

We used a subsetted Tahoe dataset and the pretrained ST-Tahoe model for a simple test. Adding embeddings worked fine using the SE-600M model, but inferring with the ST-Tahoe model resulted in several issues, listed below:

1. RuntimeError during inference via CLI

When using the command-line interface to run inference from a checkpoint, we encountered the following runtime error early in processing:
```
RuntimeError: shape '[1, -1, 2000]' is invalid for input of size 526848
```
This occurs at line 297 of 'state/src/state/tx/models/pert_sets.py':

```python
basal = batch["ctrl_cell_emb"].reshape(1, -1, self.input_dim)
```
The command used was:
```
state tx infer --output . --model_dir ./ST-Tahoe --checkpoint ./ST-Tahoe/final.ckpt --adata embedded_control_10conditions.h5ad --pert_col drugname_drugconc --embed_key X_state
```


2. Issues with `load_model(self, checkpoint)` from `src/state/emb/inference.py`

We then tried to load the ST-Tahoe model directly using the `load_model` function. However, the checkpoint `./ST-Tahoe/final.ckpt` appears to be missing several required fields in its `hyper_parameters` section:
  `token_dim`, `d_model`, `nhead`, `d_hid`, and `nlayers`.  
After manually adding these fields, inference still fails because `self.cfg.model` remains `None`.


Any insights on how to address these issues — or an example of the correct setup/configuration for inference — would be extremely helpful.

Thanks again for your outstanding work and for sharing the model with the community! We're looking forward to getting it up and running.
